title: CARRY-FORWARD r3-W2: pullback_yields app7 leg still drives effect_settings_adjust on a zeroed App - settings_save_app writes the dev's real HOME dotfile on every native test run
evidence:
app7: App
	pullback_test_app(&app7)
	defer pp.run_destroy(&app7.state)
	defer pp.catalogs_destroy(&app7.cat)
	arm_pullback(&app7)
	effect_settings_adjust(&app7, &app7.input, rnd.SETTINGS_ROW_PULLBACK, 0)
--- settings.odin ---
settings_save_app :: proc(app: ^App) {
	p := app.settings_path_override
	if p == "" {
		p = settings_path()
	}
	settings_save_at(p, app.a11y)
}
detail: The zeroed fixture leaves settings_path_override empty, so the toggle persists auto_pullback=OFF to the real ~/.pp-settings.bin — the exact write settings_save_app's own comment forbids. Deterministic, not hypothetical.
recommended_fix: Set app7.settings_path_override to a temp path (the exec-level adjust-test pattern) before effect_settings_adjust; delete the temp on exit.

title: CARRY-FORWARD r3-W3: pullback_feed caps the spawn-event mapping at ids[8] - a frame with 9+ NODE_SPAWNED events hits found != n_spawns and silently skips the pullback
detail: camera_newest_terminals breaks at len(ids)=8, found returns 8 != n_spawns, and the whole frame's seeds are dropped with no log. Unreachable at interval 80, but the interval is balance.json data.
recommended_fix: Clamp n_spawns to the buffer size and map the OLDEST 8 (newest-first walk order keeps a truncated mapping correct for the newest seed), or size the buffer to the max same-frame spawns.

title: CARRY-FORWARD r3-W4: the same-window exclusion's correctness still silently depends on terminal_spawn_interval_ticks exceeding the per-frame tick cap - no assertion anywhere
evidence:
window_lo := ids[n_spawns - 1]
	window_hi := ids[0] + 1
--- growth.odin ---
	// (terminal_spawn_interval_ticks — 80 = 4 s @ 20 Hz, the 2× reduction).
detail: At interval <= ticks-per-frame two spawns share a frame; the frame-level exclusion then hides the first spawn from the second's classification, diverging view SEED detection from plan-time. Inert today, wrong when the data knob moves.
recommended_fix: Assert the invariant where balance loads (interval > max ticks per frame), or derive the exclusion window from the interval instead of the frame slice.

title: CARRY-FORWARD r3-N10: wheel residue advances in poll_mouse before the ownership decision - notches consumed as Noc_Scroll/Blocked pre-charge the accumulator
detail: The only residue write is the poll; a notch scrolled over the NOC panel or blocked by the modal leaves residue 0.2-0.9 armed, so the first map wheel afterwards fires one notch early. Cosmetic bias, never spontaneous.
recommended_fix: Reset wheel_accum to 0 when the policy consumes a notch as Noc_Scroll or Blocked, or document the carry as accepted.

title: CARRY-FORWARD r3-N1: the stale-latch guard appends a synthetic Mouse_Release without clearing inp.panning - with placement armed the pan branch is gated off and a release is synthesized every frame
detail: The only latch-clearing path (pan branch) requires placing_eff < 0; a stranded latch plus an armed placement (pad tray arm + missed release) emits a synthetic release every frame, feeding Place_Release intents repeatedly.
recommended_fix: Clear inp.panning inside the stale-guard branch before appending the synthesized release — the release's purpose is closing the latch.

title: CARRY-FORWARD r3-N9: the Pan executor case still has no drag guard - a two-finger pan fires mid touch-draw and pans the camera under the live gesture
detail: mouse_map emits Pan only when !drag_eff; the executor routes every Pan unconditionally, so a second finger during a touch draw pans mid-gesture (preview re-snaps; commit uses node ids — worst case jitter). The new comment still doesn't declare co-fire intent.
recommended_fix: Either suppress Pan while inp.drag.active in the executor or extend the case comment to declare the co-fire intentional.
